summary: Adders, multiplexers and decoders are the blocks every processor and FPGA design is built from. You derive the full adder, show why ripple-carry delay grows with word length, derive carry look-ahead from generate and propagate terms, and simulate both at gate level with timing for all 256 input pairs.
html:
Building blocks

  • Multiplexer: selects one of 2k inputs using k select lines; a 2:1 mux is Y=S′A+SB.
  • Decoder: turns a k-bit code into one of 2k active outputs, used for chip selects and address decoding.
  • Full adder: adds bits a, b and carry-in c:
s=a⊕b⊕c,cout​=ab+c(a⊕b).

Define generate g=ab (this bit makes a carry by itself) and propagate p=a⊕b (it passes an incoming carry on). Then cout​=g+pc and s=p⊕c.

Ripple carry versus look-ahead

A ripple-carry adder chains n full adders. Each carry waits for the previous one, two gate delays per bit (an AND then an OR), so delay grows linearly: t≈2n gate delays.

Carry look-ahead expands the recursion so every carry depends only on the g, p terms and c0​:

c1​=g0​+p0​c0​,c2​=g1​+p1​g0​+p1​p0​c0​,c3​=g2​+p2​g1​+p2​p1​g0​+p2​p1​p0​c0​.

Each carry is a two-level sum of products, so all carries are ready after about 3 gate delays regardless of position. The price is gates with many inputs; real designs use 4-bit look-ahead blocks arranged hierarchically, giving delay that grows like logn.

Worked example

Add 1111+0001 (15 + 1), the worst case for ripple carry, with one unit of delay per gate (multi-input gates count as one).

  1. At t=1: p=1110 and g=0001.
  2. Ripple: c1​ is ready at t=3, c2​ at 5, c3​ at 7, so s3​=p3​⊕c3​ settles at t=8. The carry out appears at t=9.
  3. Look-ahead: every ci​ is ready at t=3, so all sum bits are done at t=4.
  4. Scaled up: a 32-bit ripple adder at 20 ps per gate needs about 2×32×20=1.28 ns, limiting the clock to about 780 MHz before anything else in the path is counted.

Code it from scratch

adders.py
def full_adder_timed(a, b, c):
    """Each input is (value, arrival time); every gate adds 1 unit of delay."""
    p = (a[0] ^ b[0], max(a[1], b[1]) + 1)
    g = (a[0] & b[0], max(a[1], b[1]) + 1)
    pc = (p[0] & c[0], max(p[1], c[1]) + 1)
    cout = (g[0] | pc[0], max(g[1], pc[1]) + 1)
    s = (p[0] ^ c[0], max(p[1], c[1]) + 1)
    return s, cout

def ripple(a, b, n=4):
    c, out = (0, 0), []
    for i in range(n):
        s, c = full_adder_timed(((a >> i) & 1, 0), ((b >> i) & 1, 0), c)
        out.append(s)
    return out, c

def lookahead(a, b, n=4, c0=0):
    p = [((a >> i) & 1) ^ ((b >> i) & 1) for i in range(n)]
    g = [((a >> i) & 1) & ((b >> i) & 1) for i in range(n)]
    carries = [(c0, 0)]
    for i in range(1, n + 1):                    # c_i = g_{i-1} + p_{i-1} g_{i-2} + ... + p_{i-1}..p_0 c0
        terms = []
        for j in range(i):                       # term: g_j * p_{j+1} ... p_{i-1}
            t = g[j]
            for k in range(j + 1, i):
                t &= p[k]
            terms.append(t)
        t = c0
        for k in range(i):
            t &= p[k]
        terms.append(t)
        carries.append((int(any(terms)), 3))     # g/p at 1, AND level at 2, OR level at 3
    sums = [(p[i] ^ carries[i][0], max(1, carries[i][1]) + 1) for i in range(n)]
    return sums, carries[n]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    worst_r = worst_l = 0
    for a in range(16):
        for b in range(16):
            for adder in (ripple, lookahead):
                s, c = adder(a, b)
                assert sum(bit << i for i, (bit, _) in enumerate(s)) + (c[0] << 4) == a + b
            worst_r = max(worst_r, max(t for _, t in ripple(a, b)[0]))
            worst_l = max(worst_l, max(t for _, t in lookahead(a, b)[0]))
    s, c = ripple(15, 1)
    print(f"15 + 1 ripple: sum bit times {[t for _, t in s]}, carry out at {c[1]}; look-ahead worst {worst_l}")
    assert [t for _, t in s] == [2, 4, 6, 8] and c[1] == 9 and worst_r == 8 and worst_l == 4
    assert abs(2 * 32 * 20e-12 - 1.28e-9) < 1e-18

Exercises

Write the 4:1 multiplexer as a sum of products with selects S1​S0​ and inputs D0​–D3​.

Show the solution

Y=S1′​S0′​D0​+S1′​S0​D1​+S1​S0′​D2​+S1​S0​D3​.

How many gate delays does a 16-bit ripple adder need in this model, and how many for 4-bit look-ahead blocks rippling between blocks?

Show the solution

Ripple: the top sum bit at 2×16=32. With four 4-bit look-ahead blocks, each block’s carry out takes about 2 extra delays once its carry in is known (about 3 for the first), so roughly 3+2×3+1=10, about a third.

How many select lines does a 16:1 multiplexer need?
quiz.explain: 2k inputs need k selects.
